newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF allowed to hold long-term JGBs until maturity.
newsitem.headline: MOF allowed to hold long-term JGBs until maturity.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance's (MOF) Trust Fund Bureau can now hold long-term Japanese government bonds it buys regularly from the secondary market until maturity, a MOF official said on Wednesday.

The bureau's plan to buy 2.4 trillion yen worth of long-term JGBs in fiscal 1997/98 was approved by the parliament last month, enabling the bureau to hold long-term JGBs for five years and longer, he said.
Earlier in the afternoon, the JGB market rallied on a Nihon Keizai Shimbun report that the bureau will shift its investment focus to holding JGBs for five years and longer.
The bureau has been buying 100 billion yen worth of long-term JGBs from the secondary market twice a month since June 1996. The bonds have been only 10-year JGBs, traders said.
But until March 31, because the bureau did not have parliamentary approval, it was only allowed to hold long-term JGBs for a period of up to five years, the MOF official said.
On April 1, the Bureau bought 15 issues of 10-year JGBs worth a total of 100 billion yen, the first such purchase since fiscal 1997/98 started.
"We received parliamentary approval which allows us to hold JGBs until maturity, depending on market conditions," the MOF official said.
